diagnosis.question: Why do warm, email-having users who arrive in the create app leave the very first (welcome) screen without picking a role - the heaviest single sub-drop, ~37% even among the warmest claim-forwarded users?
hypotheses_considered: Competing exit CTA / 'you're done' signal: for claim users the welcome header is rewritten to LEAD with a loud green '✅ YOUR 30% OFF CODE IS ON ITS WAY / We sent your code to {email} / Not in your inbox? Check your spam folder. / While you wait...' - the first and loudest thing tells them their reason for scanning is handled and literally points them at their email app.
Value ceiling: the video is an unannounced bonus never promised on the box; some arrivals simply never wanted a video and leave once the discount is handled (a ceiling no header reorder moves).
Silent demo: the welcome clip autoplays muted with a 'Tap for sound' overlay, so the payoff never lands for the ~66% who don't tap (Angle 1 territory).
Decision friction at the role fork itself (cold identity question).
diagnosis.evidence_gathered: PostHog person-linked funnels both windows (frozen with --until); HogQL person counts for arrived (87) and role-selected (48), and the same split by from_claim (claim 38/60=63%, non-claim 14/32=44%); PostHog session_recordings API for 2026-07-18..08-01 - inspected metadata for 31 app-start recordings and deduped to 15 distinct claim-forwarded app arrivals (12 of 15 left within <=6 active seconds with zero clicks/keys; only 3 interacted, those with 25-37 active seconds and multiple clicks); read the exact claim-arrival header markup in index.html lines 1611-1642; review-click phase breakdown for both 14d windows and 30d (in-app thank-you 89%, email_redirect 0).
diagnosis.what_the_evidence_supports: The loss is LOCATED precisely: it happens at first paint on the in-app welcome, fast (<=6s) and before any interaction, and the header block a claim user sees first at that moment is the code-status + 'check your spam' + 'while you wait' block. That is a real, observable, self-inflicted competing CTA sitting exactly where and when the loss occurs. The change that historically moved this funnel was a structural in-app-entry change, matching this lever.
diagnosis.what_it_cannot_distinguish: A fast silent exit is consistent with BOTH the competing-CTA/'done-signal' cause AND the value-ceiling cause (a user who never wanted the video leaves just as fast). The instruments cannot separate 'the done-signal pushed them out' from 'they never wanted the bonus' - both produce identical <=6s zero-interaction metadata, and the welcome screen has no scroll/focus micro-events between paint and role-select. Also, claim-forwarded users actually pick a role at a HIGHER rate (63%) than non-claim (44%), which does not by itself prove the block helps or hurts (populations differ in intent) but does mean the block is not catastrophic. So the cause is under-determined, not contradicted - this fix is an honest bet on the done-signal mechanism, defensible because even under the ceiling reading, removing a competing exit CTA and leading with the invitation cannot hurt and gives the marginal user a reason to stay.

plan.title: Quiet the inbox exit: lead the claim-arrival welcome with the invitation, demote the 'code is on its way / check your spam' block to one calm confirmation line
plan.targets: In-app entry (index.html welcome): claim-forwarded users, arrived -> pick a role -> reach Create
plan.mechanism: For claim-forwarded users (from=claim), the welcome header is currently rewritten to LEAD with the loudest possible reason to leave: a big green uppercase '✅ YOUR 30% OFF CODE IS ON ITS WAY', 'We sent your code to {email}', 'Not in your inbox? Check your spam folder.' (a literal instruction to switch to the email app), then a 'While you wait...' eyebrow (idle-filler framing) ABOVE the create invitation. This re-ranks that block: the create invitation ('Turn your gift into a video they'll love' + a warm, non-emoji-soup value line) becomes the first and loudest element, and the code status is demoted to a single slim, low-emphasis confirmation line that KEEPS the reassurance ('30% off code on its way to {email}') but drops the 'check your spam folder' competing CTA (redundant - the spam reassurance already appears on the final 'Check your email' screen at index.html:1304 and :1749, i.e. at the moment it's actually needed) and the 'While you wait...' idle framing. Net effect: the first thing a fast-glancing arrival processes is a reason to STAY and create, not a 'you're done, go check your inbox' signal.
plan.assumed_cause: The loud, top-of-screen code-status + 'check your spam' + 'while you wait' block acts as a competing exit CTA / 'you're already done' signal at first paint, so a slice of the ~37% who leave the welcome screen within seconds are being given permission and a destination to leave before they ever consider making the video.

cause_verification.for: Read the exact markup (index.html:1621-1634): the claim-arrival header literally leads with '✅ YOUR 30% OFF CODE IS ON ITS WAY' + 'Check your spam folder' + 'While you wait...' above the invitation - the flaw is in the code, not a guess about feelings. Session replay localizes the loss to exactly this moment: of 15 distinct claim-forwarded app arrivals with recordings in-window, 12 left within <=6 active seconds with zero clicks and zero keypresses - a fast, pre-interaction exit driven by whatever is visible at first paint, which is this block at the top.
cause_verification.against: I actively looked for evidence that would CONTRADICT the done-signal cause: (1) I watched WHEN bounces happen expecting that if the block were irrelevant, exits would cluster later (after engaging the role fork or video) - instead they cluster at <=6s before any interaction, consistent with a first-paint signal, not refuting it. (2) I segmented role-selection by from_claim to test whether users who SEE this block convert worse than users who don't: claim-forwarded users convert HIGHER (63%, 38/60) than non-claim who never see the block (44%, 14/32). This is the one finding that cuts against a strong 'the block repels people' story - but it is confounded (claim users are warmer, having just paid the email price), so it shows the block is not catastrophic rather than that it is harmless. (3) The honest limit I could NOT overturn: a <=6s silent exit is equally consistent with a pure video-interest ceiling; the instruments have no micro-events between paint and role-select to separate the two.
cause_verification.why_for_wins: The cause is under-determined, not contradicted - nothing I found disproves it, and the flaw is a real, observable, self-inflicted competing CTA sitting exactly where and when the loss occurs. It is worth betting on because the fix is asymmetric: even if the true driver is a value-ceiling rather than the done-signal, removing a 'go check your email' instruction and an idle-filler eyebrow and leading with the invitation cannot reduce role-selection and gives the marginal, undecided arrival a reason to stay. Unlike the last failed cycle (which proposed a fix for a cause the session data actively DISPROVED), here the session data confirms the loss is at first paint where this block lives, and the change is reversible, on-brand, and touches no gate/reward/promise.

plan.why_the_rate_is_what_it_is: This step is NOT an exchange - these users have already paid the price (submitted their email, received the discount promise) and were auto-forwarded in. There is nothing left for them to 'give up'; the only question is motivation to spend a minute on an unannounced bonus. So the rate is a pure motivation/attention outcome, and the current screen spends its most valuable real estate (first paint, top, loudest) telling them the thing they came for is handled and pointing them away - actively lowering the motivation it should be raising.
what_would_have_to_be_true: A non-trivial share of the fast silent exiters are responding to the 'you're done / go check email' signal rather than being pure video-ceiling (unprovable at this traffic; the bet).
The create invitation, when it is the first/loudest element, is compelling enough to earn a role tap from an undecided arrival.

Demoting (not removing) the code confirmation does not break the discount promise - satisfied because a slim confirmation line is retained and the spam reassurance still appears on the final 'Check your email' screen where it's actually needed.
plan.second_order_effects: Downstream review machinery is untouched: email is already captured on claim.html BEFORE this screen, the code is still sent by Klaviyo, and the video is still delivered by email - so nothing that feeds the review-reminder path changes (measured: phase=email_redirect review clicks = 0 in both 14d windows and 0 over 30d, so there is no email-reminder review volume to put at risk here anyway). One step further: the only plausible harm is a user who ONLY wanted the discount being momentarily less reassured their code is coming - mitigated by keeping an explicit one-line 'code on its way to {email}' confirmation and by the unchanged spam note on the final screen. If MORE warm users stay and finish videos, that increases load on the in-app thank-you review ask (the 89% engine) - the intended effect.
plan.strongest_case_against: A sceptic would say: 'You proved people leave in <=6s with zero interaction - that is the signature of someone who never wanted the video, a ceiling. Reordering a header will not create desire that isn't there, and claim users already convert BETTER (63%) than non-claim (44%), so the block clearly isn't the problem. This is presentation polish dressed up as a fix, and at ~60 arrivals/fortnight you can never prove it either way.' My honest answer: I concede the cause is a bet and cannot be proven at this traffic (measurable:false, and I will never claim it worked without a SIGNIFICANT result). But the sceptic's own evidence - a decision made at first paint - is precisely why the first-paint content matters: if the loudest first thing is 'you're done, go check your email,' you are converting undecided arrivals into leavers at the exact instant they decide. The 63%>44% gap is confounded by intent (claim users are warmer) and shows only that the block is not catastrophic, not that it is optimal. The fix is cheap, reversible, on-brand, breaks no promise, and is asymmetric (cannot lower role-selection), so it is exactly the small compounding bet this job exists to make - and it is the structural in-app-entry KIND of change that historically moved this funnel (+14pts, 2026-06-16), not the claim-page reshuffle KIND that went flat.
plan.expected_effect: A few points of extra arrived->role among claim-forwarded users, flowing downstream to a few more finished videos and thus more in-app thank-you review clicks (the 89% engine). Directionally positive; below the noise floor at this traffic.

tradeoff.gained: Removes a self-inflicted competing exit CTA at the highest-value warm-user drop; leads with a reason to stay and create, feeding the dominant (89%) review engine.
tradeoff.risked: Slightly less prominence on the 'your code is coming / check spam' reassurance for a user who only wanted the discount - mitigated by retaining a one-line code confirmation and by the unchanged spam reassurance on the final 'Check your email' screen. Downstream review-reminder volume is not at risk: email is captured upstream and phase=email_redirect review clicks = 0 in both 14d windows and 0 over 30d.
unverified_assumptions: Whether the fast <=6s silent exiters are responding to the done-signal vs a pure video-interest ceiling cannot be separated with current instruments (no micro-events between paint and role-select).

plan.differs_from_past_attempt: The only prior in-app-entry attempt (2026-06-16) ADDED a value-prop text hero + a 'Free / Takes a minute / No app needed' cost line ABOVE the role cards - it never touched the code-status/'check your spam'/'while you wait' block that competes with the ask (in fact that hero copy currently sits BELOW the loud code block). This change re-ranks the hierarchy so the invitation leads and demotes/removes the competing inbox-exit CTA - a structural change to the same screen, distinct mechanism. It is on index.html, unrelated to the claim-page 07-23 imagery/voice work and to PR #8's claim-page reshuffle. It touches neither owner rejection: no discount code is handed over before the email (email was already given upstream), and it never references the printed percentage.
plan.how_to_verify: Boot the app (PORT=3939 node --experimental-websocket server.js) and load index.html?sku=PTT-GREEN1&from=claim&branch=receiver&email=test@example.com: confirm the create invitation ('Turn your gift into a video they'll love' + warm value line) is the first/loudest header element, the code status is a single slim confirmation line retaining {email}, and 'Not in your inbox? Check your spam folder.' and 'While you wait...' are gone from the arrival header (spam note still present on the final Check-your-email screen). Render mobile before/after PNGs to check the hierarchy reads premium/warm and not childish. Re-measure ~2026-08-15 with PostHog in-app funnel (page_view page=main -> role -> Create Video Button Clicked -> Video Creation Started, --until frozen) segmented by from_claim, then significance-test; label any read honestly and never claim 'worked' without a SIGNIFICANT tools/significance.mjs result.
alternatives_rejected: Angle 1 'Payoff-first hero' (captioned auto-playing example as the hero): higher ceiling and strong, but a bigger build (needs a captioned asset) and a larger bet on value-demonstration - deferred as a stronger next swing if this reads flat.

Angle 4 'Warm the role fork' / Angle 3 'Reason-to-act' / Angle 7 'Name their crochet friend': cheaper but rest more on unproven motivation/copy framing than on an observable flaw; this pick fixes a concrete, in-code competing CTA sitting exactly at the located loss.
Angle 5 'Pre-select the role from ?branch=': hinges on unverified branch reliability for claim traffic and edges toward removing a decision - held pending verification.
Claim gate (landed->email): recently attacked twice (07-23) and near-zero downstream review value (email_redirect 0/19 over 30d) - lower value-to-reviews than the in-app entry.
